# SPD-043 — Bash hook: a command word built from a parameter expansion other than a bare variable, or a wrapper or glob reached through a variable, hides the command (Law 7)

## Brief
analyse_segment resolves a command word only when VARREF_RE matches it whole ($X or ${X}); ${X:-name}, ${arr[1]}, $X$Y and the like are read as other, and after a bare variable expands the prefix loop is not run again, so a wrapper it names is not stripped. A member can run a VCS write through any of them. Outside SPD-041 (globs); found probing it.

Evidence: Probed with a fake VCS binary first on a scratch PATH, zsh 5.9 -f, -o nobareglobqual, bash 3.2: ${X:-NAME} push, X=g Y=it then $X$Y push, and arr=(NAME) then ${arr[1]} push (zsh) or ${arr[0]} push (bash) each ran the fake binary with push; X=env then $X NAME push ran env with NAME push; a quoted glob in a variable (X='g?t', then $X push) ran it in bash, since bash expands an unquoted expansion's glob. analyse_command reads every one as kind other with no finding on 43de637's successor and on this branch (scratchpad holes_probe.py). Fix sketch: refuse a member when the command word holds $ or a backtick that VARREF_RE does not resolve (as SUBST is refused), and rerun the prefix loop on a resolved variable's words.
